We will describe an issue and provide three different perspectives on the issue. You are asked to read and consider the issue and perspectives, state your own perspective on the issue, and analyze the relationship between your perspective and at least one other perspective on the issue.
Issue:
Automation is generally seen as a sign of progress, but what is lost when we replace humans with machines?

Intelligent Machines
Many of the goods and services we depend on daily are now supplied by intelligent, automated machines rather than human beings. Robots build cars and other goods on assembly lines, where once there were human workers. Many of our phone conversations are now conducted not with people but with sophisticated technologies. We can now buy goods at a variety of stores without the help of a human cashier. Automation is generally seen as a sign of progress, but what is lost when we replace humans with machines? Given the accelerating variety and prevalence of intelligent machines, it is worth examining the implications and meaning of their presence in our lives.
Perspective One (Dystopian view)
What we lose with the replacement of people by machines is some part of our own humanity. Even our mundane daily encounters no longer require from us basic courtesy, respect, and tolerance for other people.
Perspective Two (Utilitarian view)
Machines are good at low-skill, repetitive jobs, and at high-speed, extremely precise jobs. In both cases they work better than humans. This efficiency leads to a more prosperous and progressive world for everyone.
Perspective Three (Progressive view)
Intelligent machines challenge our long-standing ideas about what humans are or can be. This is good because it pushes both humans and machines toward new, unimagined possibilities.

Human history is filled with examples of technological advancements leading to changes in the job market. From the industrial revolution to the rise of the internet, each new wave of technology has disrupted existing industries and created new opportunities for growth and innovation. While it is true that some jobs may become obsolete as automation and artificial intelligence continue to advance, it is also likely that new jobs and industries will emerge to take their place.

For example, as machines took over more of the manufacturing process in the 20th century, the demand for skilled workers in fields like software development and data analysis grew rapidly. Similarly, as more companies implement AI and machine learning technologies, there is a growing need for professionals who can design and manage these systems.

Instead of seeing technological advancements as a threat to jobs, we should view them as an opportunity for growth and change. By adapting to new technologies and developing new skills, individuals can position themselves to take advantage of the opportunities that arise from these changes.

Overall, the fear of widespread job loss due to automation and AI is unfounded. Historically, humans have always found ways to adapt to technological changes and create new opportunities for themselves. As long as we continue to embrace innovation and invest in education and training, there is no reason to believe that technology will lead to mass unemployment. Instead, it is simply another step in the ongoing evolution of human society.

Throughout history, technology has changed the way we work. Think about the industrial revolution and how machines replaced some jobs but created new ones. The same is happening now with automation and artificial intelligence.

Some people worry that technology will take away all our jobs. But history shows us that when jobs disappear, new ones pop up. For example, as more machines did manufacturing work, the need for computer and data experts grew.

Instead of being scared of losing jobs, we should see technology as a chance to learn new skills and find new opportunities. By adapting to new tech, we can create better jobs for ourselves.

So, don't be afraid of technology. Humans have always found ways to adapt and make the most of new inventions. As long as we keep learning and growing, we can thrive in a world with automation and AI. It's just another chapter in our story of progress.
